card: This PR inlines CBlockIndexWorkComparator and arith_uint256 comparisons into headers, streamlining them with std::tie and per-word C++20 three-way comparisons. The change removes function call and branching overhead during chain selection and CheckBlockIndex validation checks. The author reports synthetic work comparisons running roughly 6.5x faster and CheckBlockIndex running 1.4x to 1.6x faster on GCC and Clang, though CheckBlockIndex is disabled by default on mainnet. No dependencies are stated.
changed_since_previous: Dropped the dedicated microbenchmarks and differential fuzz targets that were present in the earlier revision, keeping only the refactoring commits and targeted unit tests.
evidence: PR description: synthetic 256-bit work comparisons are 6.51x to 6.80x faster across GCC and Clang, and CheckBlockIndex is 1.39x to 1.62x faster.
problem: Block index ordering in chain selection and `CheckBlockIndex()` calls `CBlockIndexWorkComparator` and `arith_uint256::CompareTo` frequently. Because both were defined out-of-line and relied on manual branching comparisons, callers suffered function call and branch overhead.

risk.why: A flaw in chain work comparison or tie-break ordering could cause nodes to select the wrong active chain tip and split consensus.

summary: Inlines block index comparators and `arith_uint256` comparisons into header files, marking them `noexcept`. Replaces the manual branching in `CBlockIndexWorkComparator` with a single `std::tie` tuple comparison and replaces out-of-line `base_uint::CompareTo` with an inlined per-word `operator<=>` loop. Adds unit tests pinning arithmetic comparison word precedence and block index tie-break ordering.
